sources.fullCitation: “O chant d'amour de Tahiti ! : chanson tahitienne : du film ‘Les révoltés du Bounty’ / B. Kaper, W. Jurmann, G. Rey, comp.” Coupled with “Ho'i-maï : mélodie tahitienne / G. Rey, comp. et par.” Performed by Tihoti-ré et son ensemble tahitien, vocal duo by Mlle Maéva and Tihoti, presented by E. Ventrillon. Paris: Industries Musicales et Electriques Pathé-Marconi, 1940. One 78 rpm disc, 25 cm, Pathé PA 1234, matrices CPT 3351 and CPT 3352. Catalogued by the Bibliothèque nationale de France with the language given as Tahitian. Accessed 1 August 2026.

sources.shortCitation: BnF person authority record for Georges Rey
sources.fullCitation: Bibliothèque nationale de France, notice de personne “Rey, Georges (1908-2011)”, forme internationale, FRBNF16974300. Born 27 May 1908 in Papeete, Tahiti; died 6 January 2011 in Bazas, Gironde. Described as a Tahitian composer, singer and musician who worked as an assistant book-keeper in an American camp in the Gironde, and known also under the pseudonym Tihoti-Ré, or Tihoti-Re. The notice cites as its sources the Pathé disc of “O chant d'amour de Tahiti !” and Claude Lestrade, “Quelques souvenirs de Tahiti de 1942 à 1945 (2e partie),” Journal de la Société des océanistes 95 (1992), pp. 251–274. Accessed 1 August 2026.
sources.title: Rey, Georges (1908-2011) — notice de personne
sources.creator: Bibliothèque nationale de France

contributions.scopeNote: Credited as composer alongside Kaper and Jurmann on the Tahitian-language version issued by Pathé-Marconi in 1940 as “O chant d'amour de Tahiti !” (Pathé PA 1234), not on the 1935 song. The Bibliothèque nationale de France distinguishes the roles deliberately on this disc: the coupling, “Ho'i-maï”, is credited to Rey as “comp. et par.”, while the Tahiti side gives all three men “comp.” and names no lyricist. Rey also performs on the record, leading Tihoti-ré et son ensemble tahitien and singing the vocal duo with Mlle Maéva under his Tahitian pseudonym Tihoti.

personNameVariants.publicNote: Tahitian pseudonym, given in the BnF person authority record as Tihoti-Ré or Tihoti-Re, with a see-also reference under that form. Tihoti is the Tahitian rendering of Georges. The Pathé disc credits the performing group as Tihoti-ré et son ensemble tahitien and names Tihoti in the vocal duo, so the composer credited as G. Rey and the singer credited as Tihoti are the same man.
